args.changes_since_last_round: Initial round of hypotheses based on observability and dependency findings.

assumptions: Limit orders comprise roughly 35% of total order submissions in orders-service.
The NullPointerException is caused by an unhandled null object or missing null check introduced in the refactored validation logic or new quote client.

checks.description: Examine git diff for orders-service v4.18.0 (dep-0009) specifically in LimitPriceValidator.java around lines 82-90 to identify the null dereference.
Perform rollback of orders-service from v4.18.0 to v4.17.3 to verify if HTTP 500 errors and LimitPriceValidator NullPointerExceptions cease.

hypotheses.mechanism: Deployment dep-0009 rolled out orders-service version 4.18.0 between 2026-03-10T10:08:00Z and 10:12:00Z, which refactored LimitPriceValidator and switched to a new quote client. As new pods began receiving traffic at 10:11:00Z, order submissions requiring limit-price validation triggered a NullPointerException at LimitPriceValidator.java lines 82-90 (logpat-9f3348fb, log-e5f7b562e7). The unhandled exception caused requests to fail fast before database or risk processing, reducing median latency from ~45 ms to ~30 ms (met-0fa4c6a8, met-91733552) and logging internal 500 errors (logpat-bfde8c2f, log-900b776c85). This caused ~35% of orders to fail (met-64d320dc), and upstream api-gateway received HTTP 500 responses for POST /api/v1/orders (logpat-a78fdc98, log-a888097ce7), resulting in an elevated api-gateway error rate of ~10-13% (met-e8e7fccd, met-83b2a04b).
hypotheses.title: Regression in LimitPriceValidator shipped in orders-service v4.18.0 deployment

assumptions: quotes-service is returning 200 OK responses with empty/null payload bodies for specific quotes, which does not register as an error on quotes-service error_rate_pct.

checks.description: Inspect request/response logs and payload bodies between orders-service and quotes-service for quote lookups during order validation between 10:11 and 10:30 UTC.

hypotheses.mechanism: quotes-service began returning null quote data or empty payload structures for a subset of instruments. When orders-service attempts to validate limit prices against quotes-service data (topo-orders-service), LimitPriceValidator encounters a null quote reference and throws NullPointerException (logpat-9f3348fb, log-e5f7b562e7), returning HTTP 500 to api-gateway (logpat-a78fdc98).
hypotheses.title: quotes-service returning null quote data leading to validator crash

assumptions: External clients or web-app began submitting order placement requests with malformed JSON or null limit price fields starting at 10:11 UTC.

checks.description: Inspect incoming POST /api/v1/orders request payloads for failing orders (such as order c7bbde44 in log-e5f7b562e7) to check if input parameters are null or malformed.

hypotheses.mechanism: A client application or user cohort began submitting order requests with null, missing, or unexpected limit price parameters at ~10:11 UTC. Inadequate input validation in orders-service causes LimitPriceValidator to throw NullPointerException when evaluating these payloads (logpat-9f3348fb, log-e5f7b562e7), returning HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 400 (logpat-bfde8c2f, logpat-a78fdc98).
hypotheses.title: Malformed order submission payload triggering unhandled null pointer in validator

open_questions: What specific line in LimitPriceValidator.java (lines 82-90) threw the NullPointerException, and does it dereference a quote object from the new quote client or a field in the order entity?
Can orders-service be immediately rolled back to version 4.17.3 to mitigate customer impact?
args.ranking_rationale: H1 is ranked first with high confidence (0.85) because deployment dep-0009 explicitly refactored limit-price validation and introduced a new quote client between 10:08 and 10:12 UTC, directly matching the 10:11 UTC onset of NullPointerExceptions in LimitPriceValidator.java (logpat-9f3348fb). Downstream services (quotes-service, orders-db, risk-service, event-bus) are verified healthy with baseline metrics. H2 (0.10) considers a dependency failure where quotes-service returns null responses, but quotes-service metrics show normal error rates (met-8fa3f53e) and no changes were made to it. H3 (0.05) considers bad client input data, but is contradicted by the exact temporal alignment with dep-0009 and the absence of validator errors prior to 10:11 UTC across steady request traffic (met-34108da2).

args.executive_summary: Roughly 35% of order submission requests (POST /api/v1/orders) began failing with HTTP 500 at 10:11 UTC, causing elevated upstream error rates on api-gateway. The failure is caused by a software regression introduced in orders-service deployment dep-0009 (v4.18.0), which refactored limit-price validation and switched to a new quote client. Starting at 10:11 UTC, orders-service threw unhandled NullPointerExceptions in LimitPriceValidator.validate on limit orders, causing immediate request termination. We are highly confident (confidence 0.85) in this root cause as downstream dependencies (quotes-service, orders-db, risk-service) remain completely healthy with stable baseline metrics. The immediate priority action is to roll back orders-service from v4.18.0 to v4.17.3 to restore order processing.

facts.text: orders-service deployment dep-0009 (v4.18.0) rolled out between 2026-03-10T10:08:00Z and 10:12:00Z with changes refactoring limit-price validation and switching to a new quote client.
At 2026-03-10T10:11:00Z, orders-service logged the first occurrence of NullPointerException in LimitPriceValidator.validate(LimitPriceValidator.java:82).
orders-service logged 600 occurrences of NullPointerException in LimitPriceValidator.validate and 600 internal error 500 failures between 10:11:00Z and 10:30:59Z.
At 2026-03-10T10:11:06Z, api-gateway began logging upstream 500 errors from orders-service for POST /api/v1/orders requests, accumulating 400 warnings.
orders-service error rate spiked sharply from a 0.3% baseline to over 30%, peaking at 42.8% starting at 10:11 UTC.
api-gateway error rate jumped from 0.3% to 9.8%, peaking at 13.1% starting at 10:11 UTC.
orders-service median latency (latency_p50_ms) dropped from 44.8 ms to 29.8 ms at 10:11 UTC.
Downstream dependencies quotes-service, risk-service, orders-db, and event-bus remained healthy with baseline error rates and stable connection counts throughout the incident.
orders-service request rate (~120 rps), CPU utilization (~35%), and DB pool wait times (~2 ms) remained steady with no signs of resource exhaustion.

assumptions: Limit orders comprise roughly 35% of total order submissions in orders-service.
The NullPointerException is caused by an unhandled null object or missing null check introduced in the refactored validation logic or new quote client.
hypotheses.mechanism: Deployment dep-0009 rolled out orders-service version 4.18.0 between 2026-03-10T10:08:00Z and 10:12:00Z, which refactored LimitPriceValidator and switched to a new quote client. As new pods began receiving traffic at 10:11:00Z, order submissions requiring limit-price validation triggered a NullPointerException at LimitPriceValidator.java lines 82-90 (logpat-9f3348fb, log-e5f7b562e7). The unhandled exception caused requests to fail fast before database or risk processing, reducing median latency from ~45 ms to ~30 ms (met-0fa4c6a8, met-91733552) and logging internal 500 errors (logpat-bfde8c2f, log-900b776c85). This caused ~35% of orders to fail (met-64d320dc), and upstream api-gateway received HTTP 500 responses for POST /api/v1/orders (logpat-a78fdc98, log-a888097ce7), resulting in an elevated api-gateway error rate of ~10-13% (met-e8e7fccd, met-83b2a04b).
hypotheses.title: Regression in LimitPriceValidator shipped in orders-service v4.18.0 deployment

assumptions: quotes-service is returning 200 OK responses with empty or null payload bodies for specific quotes, which does not register as an error on quotes-service error_rate_pct.
hypotheses.mechanism: quotes-service began returning null quote data or empty payload structures for a subset of instruments. When orders-service attempts to validate limit prices against quotes-service data (topo-orders-service), LimitPriceValidator encounters a null quote reference and throws NullPointerException (logpat-9f3348fb, log-e5f7b562e7), returning HTTP 500 to api-gateway (logpat-a78fdc98).
hypotheses.title: quotes-service returning null quote data leading to validator crash

assumptions: External clients or web-app began submitting order placement requests with malformed JSON or null limit price fields starting at 10:11 UTC.
hypotheses.mechanism: A client application or user cohort began submitting order requests with null, missing, or unexpected limit price parameters at ~10:11 UTC. Inadequate input validation in orders-service causes LimitPriceValidator to throw NullPointerException when evaluating these payloads (logpat-9f3348fb, log-e5f7b562e7), returning HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 400 (logpat-bfde8c2f, logpat-a78fdc98).
hypotheses.title: Malformed order submission payload triggering unhandled null pointer in validator

recommended_actions.description: Roll back orders-service deployment dep-0009 from version 4.18.0 to the previous stable version 4.17.3.
recommended_actions.rationale: Reverts the faulty LimitPriceValidator and quote client changes, immediately eliminating NullPointerExceptions on order submissions.

recommended_actions.description: Inspect git diff for dep-0009 in LimitPriceValidator.java (lines 82-90), fix the unhandled null dereference, add defensive null checks, and write regression tests before redeploying.
recommended_actions.rationale: Addresses the underlying defect where null quote or order fields crash the validator with an unhandled exception instead of safe handling.

recommended_actions.description: Add automated integration tests covering limit order placement validation with missing/null quote responses, and implement canary rollout validation gates monitoring error rates before 100% pod cutover.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents faulty validator logic from reaching full production traffic and automatically catches regressions prior to wide deployment.
